entries.title: Psalms 19:1
segments: is the revelation which God makes of himself in the heavens;
, the revelation which he has given in his word, with its blessed effect on those who receive and obey it.  Then

, a prayer that God would help the psalmist to be conformed, inwardly and outwardly, to this perfect rule, that he may be accepted and not put to shame before his Maker. 
 
In the creation and government of the world, the invisible things of God, even his eternal power and Godhead, may be so clearly seen, that all who do not render him spiritual homage will be without excuse.

entries.title: Psalms 19:2
segments: Day unto day--night unto night; each day and night delivers over to the succeeding day and night the work of declaring God's glory, so that the testimony of the heavens is uninterrupted from age to age.

entries.title: Psalms 19:3
segments: No speech--their voice is not heard; they do not speak in words to the ear, but to the understanding and the feelings.

entries.title: Psalms 19:4
segments: Their words; in silence speak to the hearts of those who attend to them.

entries.title: Psalms 19:7
segments:
The law of the Lord; the doctrine or truth which he has revealed. 
 
  Converting the soul; that believes and obeys it. 
 
  Making wise; all who embrace it. 
 
The written word of God is perfect as a rule of faith and practice, making all who follow it wise unto salvation; by being led to renounce all dependence upon their own righteousness, to trust alone for acceptance with God upon the atonement, righteousness, and intercession of Christ, and to seek to please him by keeping his commandments.

entries.title: Psalms 19:8
segments:
The statutes of the Lord; what he has ordained. 
 
  The commandment of the Lord; his requirements.

entries.title: Psalms 19:9
segments:
Clean; pure and purifying. 
 
  Judgments; decisions, especially judicial decisions.

entries.title: Psalms 19:10
segments: More to be desired--than gold; because true and right; making wise, excellent, useful, and happy all who follow them.

entries.title: Psalms 19:12
segments:
His errors; as seen in the light of the perfect and all-comprehensive law of God. 
 
  Secret faults; those which escape his own notice. 
 
The more men become acquainted with the Bible, and the more they are in the habit of comparing their hearts and lives with its requirements, the greater will be their conviction of the number and aggravations of their sins, and of their need of the grace, strength, and salvation of the Redeemer.

entries.title: Psalms 19:13
segments:
Presumptuous sins; committed against light and knowledge. 
 
  From the great transgression; more literally, from much transgression, such as must be the certain result of ignorance of God's law, or inattention to it.
